title: Linux Administration
description: Production Linux reference covering filesystems, permissions, users, processes, systemd, signals, networking, DNS, storage, logs, observability, packages, security, troubleshooting, and operational safety.

subtopics.title: Filesystem Layout & Paths
subtopics.description: Understand mounted filesystems rather than assuming one disk. /etc holds host configuration, /var changing state, /run volatile runtime state, /proc process/kernel views, and /sys device/kernel interfaces.

codeBlocks.code:
findmnt
df -hT
du -xhd1 /var | sort -h
stat -- /path/to/file
readlink -f -- /path/to/link

callouts.title: Deleted Files Can Still Consume Space
callouts.text: A process holding an unlinked file keeps its blocks allocated. Compare df and du and inspect open deleted files before restarting or truncating anything.

subtopics.title: Permissions, Ownership, ACLs & umask
subtopics.description: Mode bits apply to owner, group, and others; directory execute means traversal. ACLs add principals, while umask removes default permission bits.

codeBlocks.code:
namei -l /srv/app/config
install -o app -g app -m 0640 source /etc/app/config
getfacl /srv/app
setfacl -m u:operator:r-x /srv/app
umask 027

callouts.title: chmod 777 Is Not Diagnosis
callouts.text: Identify which principal needs which operation on every path component. Broad write access can turn configuration or executable paths into privilege-escalation points.

subtopics.title: Users, Groups, sudo & Capabilities
subtopics.description: Use service accounts with minimal shells and groups, audited sudo rules for administration, and narrow Linux capabilities instead of full root where supported.

codeBlocks.code:
id app
getent passwd app
getent group app
sudo -l
getcap /usr/bin/example
capsh --print

callouts.title: Edit sudoers with Validation
callouts.text: Use visudo or an equivalent validated deployment path. Grant exact commands cautiously because shells, editors, interpreters, wildcards, and writable arguments can escape intended restrictions.

subtopics.title: Processes, Threads & Resource State
subtopics.description: Inspect parentage, state, CPU, memory, file descriptors, scheduling, and cgroup placement before acting on a process.

codeBlocks.code:
ps -eo pid,ppid,user,stat,%cpu,%mem,etime,cmd --forest
top
cat /proc/<pid>/status
ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd
lsof -p <pid>
systemd-cgls

callouts.title: Load Average Is Not CPU Percentage
callouts.text: Load includes runnable tasks and typically uninterruptible waits. Compare it with CPU, I/O pressure, run queue, and workload latency.

subtopics.title: Signals, Jobs & Graceful Termination
subtopics.description: SIGTERM requests shutdown, SIGKILL cannot be handled, and job control manages processes attached to an interactive shell. Verify the exact PID or unit before signaling.

codeBlocks.code:
kill -TERM <pid>
kill -0 <pid>
jobs -l
fg %1
nohup command >app.log 2>&1 &
wait <pid>

callouts.title: Do Not Start with SIGKILL
callouts.text: SIGKILL prevents cleanup, flushes, lock release, and graceful traffic drain. Use it only after confirming shutdown is stuck and understanding data-integrity consequences.

subtopics.title: systemd Units, Dependencies & Journals
subtopics.description: Units declare service lifecycle, dependencies, isolation, restart policy, credentials, and resource limits. Enable controls boot behavior; start controls current state.

codeBlocks.code:
systemctl status app.service
systemctl cat app.service
systemctl show app.service -p MainPID -p Restart -p MemoryCurrent
journalctl -u app.service --since -1h
systemd-analyze security app.service

callouts.title: Avoid Infinite Restart Storms
callouts.text: Combine deliberate Restart behavior with start-rate limits, useful exit codes, dependency readiness, and alerts. A restarting service is not necessarily healthy.

subtopics.title: Interfaces, Routes & Sockets
subtopics.description: Diagnose from link and address through route, neighbor, listening socket, firewall, transport, and application layers.

codeBlocks.code:
ip -brief link
ip -brief address
ip route get 1.1.1.1
ip neighbor
ss -lntup
ss -ntp state established

callouts.title: A Listening Socket Is Not End-to-End Reachability
callouts.text: Also verify bind address, namespace, firewall, security group, load balancer, route, TLS, application health, and return path.

subtopics.title: DNS, TLS & Connectivity Diagnostics
subtopics.description: Separate name resolution, connection establishment, TLS negotiation, and application response when troubleshooting.

codeBlocks.code:
resolvectl status
dig +trace example.com
getent ahosts example.com
curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://example.com/health
openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com </dev/null

callouts.title: dig and Applications May Resolve Differently
callouts.text: Applications may use NSS, local caches, search domains, split DNS, containers, or proxies. Reproduce resolution from the same namespace and identity as the failing service.

subtopics.title: Block Devices, Filesystems & Mounts
subtopics.description: Map block devices through partitions, encryption, volume management, filesystems, and mount options. Monitor capacity, inodes, latency, and error logs.

codeBlocks.code:
lsblk -f
findmnt -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
blkid
df -hT
df -i
iostat -xz 1

callouts.title: Filesystem Repair Requires a Runbook
callouts.text: Do not run repair tools blindly on mounted or actively used filesystems. Identify filesystem type, storage layer, backups, redundancy, and vendor guidance first.

subtopics.title: Logs, Metrics & Pressure
subtopics.description: Correlate service logs with CPU, memory, I/O, network, cgroup limits, kernel messages, and pressure-stall information over the same time window.

codeBlocks.code:
journalctl -k -p warning..alert --since today
free -h
vmstat 1
pidstat -dur 1
cat /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}
dmesg --level=err,warn

callouts.title: Check for OOM Evidence
callouts.text: A disappeared process may have been killed by the kernel or its cgroup. Inspect kernel logs, unit results, memory.events, limits, and restart history.

subtopics.title: Packages, Updates & Host Security
subtopics.description: Use signed repositories, inventory installed versions, stage security updates, minimize services, enforce MAC policy, and reboot when kernel or foundational runtime fixes require it.

codeBlocks.code:
uname -a
cat /etc/os-release
systemctl --type=service --state=running
getenforce 2>/dev/null || true
aa-status 2>/dev/null || true
find / -xdev -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null

callouts.title: Distribution Procedures Differ
callouts.text: Package commands, support windows, live patching, mandatory access control, network configuration, and service defaults vary. Follow the deployed distribution's documentation and lifecycle.

subtopics.title: Incident Workflow & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Preserve evidence, establish scope and timing, make the smallest reversible change, and record commands and outcomes while maintaining communication.

codeBlocks.code:
1. Confirm host, environment, time, and user impact
2. Capture service state, logs, metrics, recent changes, capacity
3. Form one hypothesis and run a low-risk discriminating check
4. Mitigate with a reversible bounded action
5. Verify user-facing recovery and hidden backlog/data integrity
6. Preserve timeline, root cause, and follow-up ownership

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Use least privilege, managed configuration, tested backups, time synchronization, resource limits, centralized logs/metrics, vulnerability patching, service hardening, capacity alerts, documented ownership, and rehearsed recovery.
